title: Catch Photo Log
user: An angler who takes a catch photo and needs a fast, private record of where/when it happened plus the tackle and setup facts useful on the next trip.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A fishing-journal user explicitly requests that a selected catch photo populate time, date, and location from its metadata, falling back to manual entry only when absent.
An angler trying a 100-metre trotline records line, snood, weight, target fish, lake, and fairway context while asking how to choose an anchor—trip setup is materially more than a catch count.

recurrence: Two independent 2025–2026 fishing threads require structured field capture: photo facts for one and detailed rig/site context for the other. Severity is medium because remembered details are what make a trip learnable.
current_workaround: Camera roll plus notes, spreadsheet, a social catch app, or re-entering GPS/date manually.
incumbents_and_gap: Fishbrain and Anglr emphasize community, maps, and catch feeds; generic logbooks record catches. The gap is a local photo-first session card that preserves detailed setup without exposing a fishing spot.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA that reads optional photo EXIF, then prompts for species, rig, bait/lure, water conditions, line/anchor setup, and private location precision; exports CSV/PDF.
success_measure: At least 70% of 30 trial session records retain a photo-derived time/date plus three manually chosen setup fields, with median entry time under 90 seconds.
constraints: Location must be private and removable/rounded; never advise on catch limits or anchoring safety; EXIF access requires explicit browser permission and local processing.
why_distinct: It is a private learning log for rig/context, not another public catch map or AI fish-ID wrapper.
